question: What fish evidence does Allayban et al. (2026) report for the Calay-Ab sanctuary and Calay-Ab-Sived proposed MPA, and what limits prevent app-facing use?

source.title: Reef fish community structure and biomass in a fish sanctuary and a proposed marine protected area in Ilocos Sur, Philippines
source.citation: Allayban, M. T., Ragutero, F. C., Dagdagan, J. V. P., Dela Peña, G. G., & Soliven, C. B. (2026). Reef fish community structure and biomass in a fish sanctuary and a proposed marine protected area in Ilocos Sur, Philippines. Journal of Biometry Studies, 6(1), 1–15. https://doi.org/10.61326/jofbs.v6i1.01
source.accessStatus: Publisher-hosted 15-page PDF and article metadata page reviewed online on 2026-11-19. No local article copy, table extract, figure, photo, or dataset was retained.
source.reuseStatus: The PDF states Creative Commons Attribution (CC BY), but does not state a license version in the reviewed copy. The article's tables, figures, photographs, and any underlying third-party material were not reused. Confirm component-level rights and attribution requirements before reproducing media or derived datasets.

scope.waterType: marine; coral reef; coastal sanctuary and proposed MPA context
scope.studyLocality: Calay-Ab fish sanctuary and Calay-Ab-Sived reef, Sto. Domingo, Ilocos Sur. The article says GPS was used to map the two sites and credits CENRO for its map, but the reviewed text does not provide machine-readable coordinates or a coordinate datum.
scope.collectionPeriod: One survey period; exact dates and season are not stated in the reviewed methods.
scope.samplingDesign: Underwater fish visual census using 100 m transects: two transects at the established Calay-Ab fish sanctuary and three at the proposed Calay-Ab-Sived MPA. The article describes a 5 m belt on each side, equivalent to 500 m² per transect. It also reports a separate artificial-reef assessment at the sanctuary.
scope.spatialResolution: Results are reported by the two named reef areas and by transect in tables, but no station coordinates or species-to-geographic-point crosswalk are supplied in the reviewed text. The figure is not treated as boundary or navigation geometry.
scope.taxonomicResolution: Table 4 has 43 source-listed fish-name rows and claims 18 families. Tables 5 and 6 report site counts, while Table 7 summarizes the top 20 plus an Others group. Several binomial strings vary between these tables. The review preserves this as source-reported evidence; no organism identity has been independently confirmed.

sourceReportedFindings.interpretation: These are the paper's reported reef visual-census counts and biomass estimates for one undated survey snapshot. They are not a complete regional checklist, current-presence statement, population trend, fishery landing dataset, catchability estimate, or prediction of catch.

internalConsistency.issue: The Blue-axil chromis name differs across tables: Table 4 and Tables 6–7 print Pycnchromis caudalis, while Tables 5 and 8 print Pycnochromis caudalis.
internalConsistency.disposition: Preserve each table spelling. A separate authority crosscheck may identify candidate name-string spellings but cannot identify the sampled fish without specimen or author-confirmed evidence.

internalConsistency.issue: The vermiculated angelfish is printed as Chaetodontoplus mesoleucus in Table 4 and Table 6, but as Chaetodonplus mesoleucus in Table 7.
internalConsistency.disposition: Keep source strings distinct until a separate nomenclatural crosscheck; do not silently normalize a sampled-organism row.

internalConsistency.issue: The blackbelly triggerfish is printed as Rhinecanthus verrucosus in Table 4 and Rhicanthus verrucosus in Table 6.
internalConsistency.disposition: Retain the printed strings; a spelling candidate does not verify the study identification.

internalConsistency.issue: Russell's snapper is printed as Lutjanus russelli in Table 4, Lutjanus russellii in Table 5, and Lutjanus ruselli in Table 6.
internalConsistency.disposition: Keep each source label verbatim pending an authority check and, separately, specimen-level confirmation.

internalConsistency.issue: The methods identify a single survey period but omit exact dates and season; the published summary cannot establish seasonal or year-round occurrence.
internalConsistency.disposition: Do not infer date, seasonality, or current presence.

interpretation: The paper is a useful primary marine evidence lead for two named reef study areas in Sto. Domingo. It reports a snapshot, not a complete checklist for Ilocos Sur or Region I.

Calay-Ab is described by the authors as an established fish sanctuary. Calay-Ab-Sived is explicitly a proposed MPA; this paper does not by itself establish legal boundaries, present fishing restrictions, access, or safety at either site.

The GPS/map statement does not provide usable coordinate records in the reviewed text. No point, reef polygon, sanctuary boundary, municipal-water geometry, or navigational layer is inferred from the illustration.

The paper's CC BY notice does not specify a version in the reviewed PDF. No article image, photo, map, table transcription, raw dataset, species assertion, occurrence record, or public-app row was added.

decision.reason: The primary article provides useful site- and transect-level summary counts, but its survey dates are unspecified, multiple binomial spellings conflict across tables, and the map contains no reusable georeferenced geometry in the reviewed text. Keep the record as attributed research-only evidence.

nextAction: Run a separate bounded nomenclatural crosscheck for the four table-variant taxon labels, without merging source rows or asserting the sampled organisms. Continue Region I searches across inland waters, estuaries, and other coastal study sites.
